From 5f1ef0dfcb5b7f4a91a9b0e0ba533efd9f7e2cdb Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Steven Rostedt <rostedt@goodmis.org>
Date: Mon, 5 Jan 2026 20:31:41 -0500
Subject: [PATCH] tracing: Add recursion protection in kernel stack trace
 recording

A bug was reported about an infinite recursion caused by tracing the rcu
events with the kernel stack trace trigger enabled. The stack trace code
called back into RCU which then called the stack trace again.

Expand the ftrace recursion protection to add a set of bits to protect
events from recursion. Each bit represents the context that the event is
in (normal, softirq, interrupt and NMI).

Have the stack trace code use the interrupt context to protect against
recursion.

Note, the bug showed an issue in both the RCU code as well as the tracing
stacktrace code. This only handles the tracing stack trace side of the
bug. The RCU fix will be handled separately.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/20260102122807.7025fc87@gandalf.local.home/

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Cc: Masami Hiramatsu <mhiramat@kernel.org>
Cc: Mathieu Desnoyers <mathieu.desnoyers@efficios.com>
Cc: Joel Fernandes <joel@joelfernandes.org>
Cc: "Paul E. McKenney" <paulmck@kernel.org>
Cc: Boqun Feng <boqun.feng@gmail.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20260105203141.515cd49f@gandalf.local.home
Reported-by: Yao Kai <yaokai34@huawei.com>
Tested-by: Yao Kai <yaokai34@huawei.com>
Fixes: 5f5fa7ea89dc ("rcu: Don't use negative nesting depth in __rcu_read_unlock()")
Signed-off-by: Steven Rostedt (Google) <rostedt@goodmis.org>

diff --git a/include/linux/trace_recursion.h b/include/linux/trace_recursion.h
index ae04054a1be3..e6ca052b2a85 100644
--- a/include/linux/trace_recursion.h
+++ b/include/linux/trace_recursion.h
@@ -34,6 +34,13 @@ enum {
 	TRACE_INTERNAL_SIRQ_BIT,
 	TRACE_INTERNAL_TRANSITION_BIT,
 
+	/* Internal event use recursion bits */
+	TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT,
+	TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_NMI_BIT,
+	TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_IRQ_BIT,
+	TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_SIRQ_BIT,
+	TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_TRANSITION_BIT,
+
 	TRACE_BRANCH_BIT,
 /*
  * Abuse of the trace_recursion.
@@ -58,6 +65,8 @@ enum {
 
 #define TRACE_LIST_START	TRACE_INTERNAL_BIT
 
+#define TRACE_EVENT_START	TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT
+
 #define TRACE_CONTEXT_MASK	((1 << (TRACE_LIST_START + TRACE_CONTEXT_BITS)) - 1)
 
 /*

diff --git a/kernel/trace/trace.c b/kernel/trace/trace.c
index 6f2148df14d9..aef9058537d5 100644
--- a/kernel/trace/trace.c
+++ b/kernel/trace/trace.c
@@ -3012,6 +3012,11 @@ static void __ftrace_trace_stack(struct trace_array *tr,
 	struct ftrace_stack *fstack;
 	struct stack_entry *entry;
 	int stackidx;
+	int bit;
+
+	bit = trace_test_and_set_recursion(_THIS_IP_, _RET_IP_, TRACE_EVENT_START);
+	if (bit < 0)
+		return;
 
 	/*
 	 * Add one, for this function and the call to save_stack_trace()
@@ -3080,6 +3085,7 @@ static void __ftrace_trace_stack(struct trace_array *tr,
 	/* Again, don't let gcc optimize things here */
 	barrier();
 	__this_cpu_dec(ftrace_stack_reserve);
+	trace_clear_recursion(bit);
 }
 
 static inline void ftrace_trace_stack(struct trace_array *tr,
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`include/linux/trace_recursion.h`**
   - Added five new enum constants for event-specific recursion protection:
     - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT`
     - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_NMI_BIT`
     - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_IRQ_BIT`
     - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_SIRQ_BIT`
     - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_TRANSITION_BIT`
   - Added macro `TRACE_EVENT_START` set to `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT` to define the starting bit for event recursion tracking.

2. **`kernel/trace/trace.c`**
   - Modified `__ftrace_trace_stack()`:
     - Added a call to `trace_test_and_set_recursion()` using `TRACE_EVENT_START` as the base bit. If the function returns a negative value (indicating recursion), the function exits early.
     - Added `trace_clear_recursion(bit)` at the end of the function to release the recursion bit after the stack trace is recorded.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The new recursion bits defined in `trace_recursion.h` provide a dedicated set of bits specifically for **event contexts** (normal, softirq, interrupt, NMI). Previously, only bits for general tracing recursion were available.
- The change in `trace.c` uses these new bits to protect the stack trace recording from re-entering itself when stack trace triggers are enabled. By setting the appropriate event recursion bit (using `TRACE_EVENT_START`) at the beginning of `__ftrace_trace_stack()` and clearing it at the end, the function prevents infinite recursion that could occur when stack trace events trigger other events (like RCU trace events) that might call back into the stack trace code.
- This solution specifically addresses the recursion bug on the tracing side, separating event recursion protection from existing recursion protection mechanisms.

## Summary of the Patch

This patch adds recursion protection to the kernel stack trace recording mechanism to prevent infinite recursion when stack traces are triggered from events (e.g., RCU tracing) that might re-enter the tracing system.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`include/linux/trace_recursion.h`**  
   - Added new recursion bits for event contexts:  
     `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT`, `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_NMI_BIT`, `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_IRQ_BIT`, `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_SIRQ_BIT`, `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_TRANSITION_BIT`.  
   - Defined `TRACE_EVENT_START` as the first bit in this new range (`TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT`).  
   - These bits allow per-context recursion detection for events (normal, softirq, interrupt, NMI).

2. **`kernel/trace/trace.c`**  
   - Modified `__ftrace_trace_stack()` to call `trace_test_and_set_recursion()` with `TRACE_EVENT_START` at the beginning. If recursion is detected (negative return), the function returns early without recording the stack.  
   - Added `trace_clear_recursion()` to clear the recursion bit after the stack trace is done.  
   - This ensures the stack trace code does not re‑enter itself when called from an event that might trigger another stack trace.

### Relationships Between the Changes

- The new recursion bits in the header provide the infrastructure to track recursion per interrupt context.  
- The stack trace code in `trace.c` uses these bits (specifically the interrupt context bits via `TRACE_EVENT_START`) to detect and break potential recursive loops.  
- Together, they prevent the scenario where tracing an RCU event with a stack trace trigger causes the stack trace code to call back into RCU, which then triggers another stack trace, leading to infinite recursion.  
- The patch notes that this is only the tracing side of the fix; the RCU side will be addressed separately.

2.34.1

The patch adds recursion protection for event tracing in the kernel stack trace recording path, preventing infinite recursion when tracing RCU events with stack trace triggers enabled.

## Modifications per file

### `include/linux/trace_recursion.h`
- Added five new enum bits for event-specific recursion tracking:
  - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT` (basic event context)
  - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_NMI_BIT` (NMI context)
  - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_IRQ_BIT` (interrupt context)
  - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_SIRQ_BIT` (softirq context)
  - `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_TRANSITION_BIT` (context transition)
- Defined a new macro `TRACE_EVENT_START` set to `TRACE_INTERNAL_EVENT_BIT`, used as the base bit for event recursion detection.

### `kernel/trace/trace.c`
- In `__ftrace_trace_stack`, added a call to `trace_test_and_set_recursion(_THIS_IP_, _RET_IP_, TRACE_EVENT_START)` to check and set the event recursion bit.
- If the function returns a negative value (indicating recursion is already in progress), the function returns early without recording the stack trace.
- After the stack trace is recorded, `trace_clear_recursion(bit)` is called to clear the recursion bit.

## Relationship between modifications
The new recursion bits defined in the header provide a dedicated set of recursion detection slots specifically for event contexts. The stack trace function (`__ftrace_trace_stack`) uses these bits by invoking `TRACE_EVENT_START` as its recursion threshold, ensuring that a recursive call to the stack trace (e.g., triggered by an RCU event) is detected and prevented. This avoids infinite recursion without interfering with other existing recursion protection mechanisms (e.g., for function tracing or other internal operations). The change isolates event-related recursion from other tracing contexts, directly addressing the bug where RCU callbacks re-entered the stack trace.
